title: Reconstruction of an adic module from its finite quotient tower
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I a finitely generated ideal, and for n >= 1 let A_n = A/I^n. Suppose (M_n) is an inverse system of A_n-modules such that the transition map M_{n+1}\to M_n induces an isomorphism M_{n+1}/I^n M_{n+1}\to M_n. If M = \varprojlim_n M_n, then each projection induces an isomorphism M/I^n M\to M_n, and M is I-adically complete and separated. The inverse-limit topology for the discrete modules M_n is the I-adic topology on M. [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

proof.text: Write $p_n:M=\varprojlim_jM_j\to M_n$ for the projections. The quotient hypothesis makes every transition $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ surjective, and recursively lifting an element gives a compatible element of the inverse limit, so $p_n$ is surjective. Since $I^nM_n=0$, $p_n$ kills $I^nM$ and induces a surjection $q_n:M/I^nM\to M_n$.

($M$ is $I$-adically complete; Stacks 09B7.) Let $M^\wedge=\varprojlim_nM/I^nM$ with canonical map $c:M\to M^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $r:M^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nM_n=M$ be the limit of the $q_n$. Then $r\circ c=\mathrm{id}_M$, so $M$ is an $A$-linear retract of $M^\wedge$. As $I$ is finitely generated, $M^\wedge$ is $I$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete]. The canonical map to the completion is natural, so $c_M:M\to\varprojlim_nM/I^nM$ is a retract (via $c$ and $r$) of the bijection $c_{M^\wedge}$, hence bijective: $M$ is $I$-adically complete, i.e. $c$ is bijective, and therefore $r=c^{-1}$ is bijective too.

source.place: Lemma 09B7 (lemma-limit-complete-pre), proof, with Lemma 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); invoked in the first sentence of the proof of 09B8

proof.text: (Kernels; Stacks 09B8.) Put $N_n=\ker(p_n)$. The quotient hypothesis gives that $N_{n+1}+I^nM\to N_n$ is surjective, hence $N_{n+1}/(N_{n+1}\cap I^{n+1}M)\to N_n/(N_n\cap I^nM)$ is surjective. The short exact sequences $0\to N_n/(N_n\cap I^nM)\to M/I^nM\xrightarrow{q_n}M_n\to0$ form an inverse system; by left exactness of $\varprojlim$, $\varprojlim_nN_n/(N_n\cap I^nM)=\ker(r)$, which is $0$ by the previous step. An element of a term of an inverse system with surjective transitions lifts to an element of its limit, so every $N_n/(N_n\cap I^nM)$ vanishes, i.e. $N_n\subseteq I^nM$. Since $I^nM\subseteq N_n$, $\ker(p_n)=I^nM$ and $q_n$ is injective.

source.place: Lemma 09B8 (lemma-limit-complete), proof using the kernels N_n

proof.text: The maps $q_n:M/I^nM\to M_n$ are therefore isomorphisms for all $n$. $M$ is $I$-adically complete by the second step; an element of $\bigcap_nI^nM$ maps to zero in every $M_n$ and is therefore zero, so $M$ is separated.

Because each $M_n$ is discrete, the inverse-limit topology on $M$ has the kernels $\ker(p_n)$ as a neighborhood basis of $0$. These kernels are $I^nM$ by the third step, exactly the basic neighborhoods of $0$ for the $I$-adic topology; the two topologies coincide.
